plain_english: Just as there is no difference between the real and the unreal in their own nature, so too — this is certain — there is no such difference between the inert and the non-inert.
sanskrit_cite: yathā sadasatām naiva viśeṣo 'sti nijātmani jadājaḍānām apy evaṃ nāsty asāv iti niścayaḥ

plain_english: Appearing (prakhyā) and describing (upākhyā), existence and its opposite, non-existence — none of this touches a thing's essence; that essence is what faces the knower.
sanskrit_cite: prakhyopākhyā ca sattā yad yad asattā viparyayaḥ naitat svarūpaṃ spṛśati vastuno jñātṛgāmy adaḥ

plain_english: Nor can a thing's very self be "being an object of appearing and describing" — for that would make it depend on something else, give it no single form, and break past existence itself.
sanskrit_cite: prakhyopākhyāviṣayatāpy arthasyātmā na yujyate parāpekṣitayā naikarūpatve sattvalaṅghanāt

plain_english: Granted, let there be no difference; still, from the presence and absence of appearing, a difference does get established here — and that much serves the purpose.
sanskrit_cite: mā bhūd viśeṣaḥ prakhyādibhāvābhāvau tataḥ punaḥ siddhyaty eva viśeṣo 'tra tāvatā ca prayojanam

plain_english: Even so, existence would only be fitting as tied to appearing; without reference to that, existent and nonexistent are indistinguishable.
sanskrit_cite: evam apy avabhāsānuṣaktā sattocitā bhavet tadapekṣāṃ vinā bhāvābhāvayor aviśiṣṭatā

plain_english: But how could they be indistinguishable here, when the existent performs a function (arthakriyā) and the other does not? And yet the thing, in its own self, remains without distinction.
sanskrit_cite: kathaṃ syād aviśeṣo 'tra yāvatārthakriyāṃ hi san kuryān nānyas tathāpy artho nirviśeṣo nijātmani

plain_english: So the existent thing, having taken on the limiting condition of appearing-as-functional, would exist by its own essence — yet it is not distinguished from the nonexistent.
sanskrit_cite: evam arthakriyābhāsopādhisaṃbhedam āgataḥ sann arthaḥ syāt svarūpeṇa nāsatas tu viśiṣyate

plain_english: But even there, function is not what is described in a thing whose existence is already established; the two are exactly on par — hence their grounding rests on consciousness.
sanskrit_cite: tatrāpy arthakriyā siddhasattākārthe na varṇitā samam evānayos tena pratiṣṭhā saṃvidāśrayā

plain_english: And if consciousness itself were of the form of non-grasping (aparāmarśa), then it too, in itself, would be exactly equal to the inert non-being, as before.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvid apy aparāmarśarūpā cet tad asāv api abhāvena jaḍenātha tulyaiva prāgvad ātmani
